source_title_hint: How To Fix That Muscle Knot In Your Upper Back (works better than stretching)
primary_summary: Upper‑back muscle knots arise from either excessive compression (shortened muscles) or excessive lengthening (muscles pulled apart). The root cause is often poor scapular positioning due to rounded shoulders/kyphosis, which limits rib‑cage expansion. The video proposes a two‑part corrective protocol: (1) reposition the shoulder blades onto the rib cage, and (2) improve rib‑cage expansion with a seated elbow‑on‑table exercise using a light band, a 45° arm angle, and focused breathing.
problem_statements: Muscle knots in the upper back persist after stretching or rolling because the underlying scapular position remains faulty and rib‑cage expansion is limited.

knowledge_units.title: Two mechanisms of upper‑back muscle tension
knowledge_units.summary: Muscle tension can result from (1) muscles being overly shortened and compressed, or (2) muscles being excessively lengthened, pulling their attachment sites apart.
mechanisms: Compression of muscle fibers when surrounding tissues are too short
Lengthening of muscle fibers when attachment sides are pulled away
Both mechanisms increase passive tension in the upper‑back musculature

knowledge_units.title: Elbow‑on‑table rib‑cage expansion exercise
knowledge_units.summary: A seated exercise that simultaneously repositions the scapula and trains rib‑cage expansion using a light resistance band.
execution_steps: Sit tall with sit bones balanced on both sides
Place elbows on a sturdy table, creating roughly a 45° angle between the forearm and trunk
Wrap a very light band around the wrist (optional for cueing)
Take a deep breath, allowing the rib cage to expand in all directions while maintaining the scapular position
Exhale and repeat for several repetitions, focusing on a smooth, controlled breath
Maintain the elbows on the table throughout to keep the scapula in a better resting position
cues: Feel the shoulder blades gently settle onto the rib cage
Expand the rib cage evenly with each inhale
breathing_cues: Inhale to broaden the rib cage fully
Exhale slowly, keeping the scapular position
